Inputs: $4D67 = pointer count; $4D68/$4D69 = 16-bit relocation base; split pointers at $4DAA/$4DAB for indices below $80 and $4EC2/$4EC3 for indices $80 and above

Where the relocation loop really starts. As the level is loaded, $87E3-$87E4 hold LDA #$00, so the count at $1E starts from zero here; once every pointer is done, $87EE-$87F0 write RTS ($60) over that LDA, so in a snapshot taken during play $87E3 reads RTS and $87E4 keeps the old $00.

Select the current area's recursive scene tree and render its clipped 30-by-18-cell view with palette/reflection transformations
Inputs: area index $A2; area root table $4D6A; background table $4D6B; relocated split scene pointers $4DAA/$4DAB and $4EC2/$4EC3; the scene base $4D67, added to the pointer as the immediates #$E4/#$4D at $8851 and $8856
Outputs: root pointer $02/$03 and renderer bounds/depth/offset state are initialized; recursive records are traversed and their leaves update bitmap, screen, and color work memory

Render room A in the Mansion playable phase, entering the normal scene renderer after its usual load from $A2.
Inputs: A is a valid room index; relocated scene pointers, renderer workspace, bitmap/screen/color buffers, and the active phase are initialized.
Outputs: Selects the room's scene pointer, writes its background color to $D021, traverses the scene-record tree, and renders the room.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$05, renderer scratch, and VIC-II-visible bitmap/screen/color work memory.
Hardware: Writes VIC-II background-color register $D021 and display memory; no CIA access.

Interpret and render a scene-record tree. Inputs: $02/$03 record pointer and initialized renderer workspace. Outputs: bitmap, screen, color, and traversal state are updated. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and renderer zero-page scratch. Hardware: changes hardware-visible bitmap, screen, and color RAM; no direct VIC-II register write is required.

Dispatch the current encoded scene record for the Mansion playable phase, restoring a parent record at nested terminators and returning at the outer terminator.
Inputs: $02/$03 point at the current record; $1A/$1B hold the composite origin; $38 is nesting depth; nested parent frames are on the stack.
Outputs: Decodes nonterminal records; $FF at depth zero returns, while nested $FF restores the parent frame, advances $02/$03, and continues dispatch.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$05, $1A/$1B, $25/$26, $38, renderer scratch, and restored stack bytes.
Hardware: No direct register write here; descendant rendering changes VIC-II-visible bitmap, screen-code, and color memory.

Advance over the current Mansion playable-phase scene record and resume the scene-record dispatch loop.
Inputs: $02/$03 point at a valid encoded record with length/control bits in bytes +1 and +2.
Outputs: Adds the record's encoded length to $02/$03 and tail-jumps back to scene dispatch.

Advance $02/$03 to the next encoded scene record. Inputs: $02/$03 points at a valid record header. Outputs: $02/$03 points at the following record. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, and $02/$03.

Outputs: Decodes position/reflection fields, resolves child or leaf pointers, renders the record, and advances or resumes the enclosing scene tree.

Draw the picture (scene leaf) that $04/$05 point at, for the Mansion playable phase: every leaf of a scene tree falls into it from $8911-$891B, and DrawUiImageRecord jumps to it at $B011 to draw a status-panel picture.
Inputs: $04/$05 point at the picture (first byte width and height nibbles, then its bitmap, screen and colour bytes); $25/$26 hold its column and row and $E8 bit 7 mirrors it; $E7/$DC are the clipping width and height; $02/$03 point at the record that placed it, whose byte 2 bits 5-6 give the number of colour-swap bytes that follow byte 2.
Outputs: Draws the visible cells into the bitmap, screen RAM, colour RAM and the colour copy at $0800, with the colour swaps applied; a picture wholly outside the window is skipped. Then it jumps to AdvanceSceneRecordAndContinue ($8885), which steps $02/$03 past the placing record and resumes the scene-record dispatch loop.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$09, coordinate/renderer scratch, and display work memory.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register write; it stores the bitmap, screen-code and colour bytes itself, and calls the resident compositor at $1411 for cells whose colours must be merged.

EngineEntry: The Mansion's play code starts here, from PhaseHandoff at $3FF3. It sets $AA to $FF, which lets the interrupt routine play the tune, relocates the scene pointers, clears the scene buffers, waits 25 ticks, lowers the sprite curtain over the play window (AnimateStatusPanelReveal, $1F75), draws the credits card, sets the background to black, raises the curtain again and waits until it is gone (RaiseSpriteCurtain, $8E58), which shows the card, then waits for the fire button or the second button read through the SID's pot X ($D419), keeping which in $AC, and goes on into EnterArea ($8CCF) and the main loop. Central Park's EngineEntry also sets $03CB to 1; this one leaves it alone.

Reinitialize the Mansion playable phase's scene buffers after GAME OVER and rejoin engine startup immediately before the common gameplay-entry tail. Its one caller is $8E23, reached when the last life is lost and no spare life is left.
Inputs: The death sequence has finished; resident state and the active phase occupant remain valid.
Outputs: Calls the phase scene-buffer initializer, clears $D021 to black, redraws the credit/title card (RenderCreditTitleCard, $8BDB, which clears the play window first), and continues at the engine's input/frame-loop setup at $8CB4.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, scene/gameplay initialization state, and helper scratch.
Hardware: Writes VIC-II background color $D021 and updates display/input state through the joined engine-start tail.

Set up the current area and enter the main loop, for The Mansion. This runs once each time an area is entered or redrawn, not once a frame: it is reached by falling through from the start-up wait at $8CCD, from MainTick when the redraw latch $02A9 is set ($8D7F) and after a lost life ($8DE6), and it falls into MainTick ($8D29), the per-tick loop.
Inputs: Current area $A2, the player's position and the actor/object state.
Outputs: Sets $0230=$7F; rebuilds the area's enemy meter when $012D,X holds $80-$FE and loads $022A from the area's enemy energy at $3F92; clears the play window and draws the area's scene ($9358); clears the actor slots, resets runtime state, compiles the collision records, spawns the enemy, draws inactive objects and composes the actors; on the first visit to an area below $12 sets its $011B byte and adds a score bonus ($1183 with A=$15); redraws the HUD digits, applies the area's entrance rules ($929E), stamps $026D from $E2, sets $0230=$FF and falls into MainTick.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $0230, gameplay zero page, actor/object/projectile arrays, renderer/collision scratch, and display work state.
Hardware: Through its helpers, writes $D021 and the VIC-II-visible bitmap, screen and colour memory.
The Mansion's own RenderConditionalSceneVariant ($9358): area 10 dark until its lights are on

Admit one IRQ-produced tick, run the Mansion gameplay scheduler in fixed order, and choose the next engine transition
Inputs: IRQ tick $E2 and last stamp $0268; initialized player, enemy, script, event, object, projectile, scene, and transition state
Outputs: stamps $0268; runs timing/input, player, AI, enemy animation, events, scripts, level conditions, objects, boundaries, projectiles, presentation, and resident services; then loops, restarts setup, enters death handling, or begins the level transition
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and the union of all scheduled subsystem scratch/state
The Mansion's own ServiceEnemyBoundaryLatch: hanging from the helicopter
The Mansion adds this call: the alarm lamps

Resolve the player's death in The Mansion, present the result, and select restart or GAME OVER flow. MainTick comes here when $B4 is set ($8D75); the level exit ($02AF) goes to ResolveLevelCompletion ($8E26), which MainTick jumps to directly
Inputs: death latch $B4, lives $03F2, spare-life flag $03E0 (item 8) and selected object $0279
Outputs: sets $0230=$7F and clears $B4, $B3 and $B6; clears the inactive-object display; LoseLife takes one from the lives; with lives left shows 'N LIVES LEFT' or '1 LIFE REMAINING' (counting the spare life), restores health, reloads the selected spawn and restarts at $8CCF; with none left spends the spare life if it is held, otherwise renders GAME OVER and restarts the level through ResetSceneAfterDeath ($8CA9)
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and renderer, delay, object and spawn scratch
Hardware: sets $D021=0 through LoseLife ($908D); other display changes occur through called resident/level helpers

Text "0 LIVES LEFT", drawn by the call at $8DAC that comes before it: column 9, row 8, colours $07 and $C0, then 12 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The 0 at $8DB3 is a placeholder: the instruction at $8DA9 writes the lives left (counting the spare life) plus $1B into it before the call, so the line reads 2 LIVES LEFT or more. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $8DC0.
Text 8daf plus 4, the address the instruction at $8DA9 writes: byte 4 of the table at $8DAF.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "0 LIVES LEFT" at $8DBF, and the routine that called it at $8DAC goes on.

Text "1 LIFE REMAINING", drawn by the call at $8DC3 that comes before it: column 7, row 8, colours $07 and $C0, then 16 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $8DDB.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "1 LIFE REMAINING" at $8DDA, and the routine that called it at $8DC3 goes on.

Text "GAME OVER", drawn by the call at $8E0A that comes before it: column 10, row 8, colours $07 and $F0, then 9 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $8E1B.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "GAME OVER" at $8E1A, and the routine that called it at $8E0A goes on.

ResolveLevelCompletion: runs when the completion request $02AF is set. In this level it asks for no items. Then it adds 5,000 points to the score ($1183 with A = $50: 5 to the thousands digit, 0 to the hundreds), takes away item 15 (clears $03E7), saves the items, score and clock for the next level (SaveLevelState, $1C30), counts the energy $0229 up from 0 to 21, one step each time the interrupt routine changes $022B, and jumps to the load coordinator at $16AD for the next part.

Raise the sprite curtain over the play window and wait until it is gone. Inputs: $0232 is the curtain's lower edge (a raster line, which AnimateStatusPanelReveal at $1F75 lowered) and the interrupt owns the $0231 handshake. Outputs: $0232 is reduced, two lines a frame, below $1D, sprite X expansion is disabled and $0231 is cleared, so the interrupt stops drawing the curtain. Called at the start of the game ($8CA3), after a lost life ($8DE0) and after GAME OVER ($8E1B). Clobbers: A, flags, $0231, and $0232. Hardware: writes VIC-II sprite X-expansion register $D01D.

Reset mutable Mansion engine state each time an area is set up: its one caller is $8CF7, in the area set-up routine that also runs at the start of play and after a lost life. Inputs: the active overlay and resident reset service. Outputs: timers, actor and object flags, arrays, and sentinels are restored to initial values. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and broad engine state. Hardware: none; the resident call (ResetEngineTickBaselines, $11F1) only copies the tick $E2 into $026C, $026E and $0277, and this body makes no direct I/O write.

Set up the status of a level as it starts. It clears $022B, $022C, $70, $89 and $A0, fills the 30 bytes at $3F92 that keep each area's enemy energy, and both energies ($0229, $022A) with $2C, a full bar, and sets $7A to $A4. It copies the item flags saved when the level began ($03B0-$03D7) over the live ones ($03D8-$03FF) and clears $03E9-$03F1 among them, then puts the score ($1CA0) and the clock's digits back from the saved copy ($03CC-$03D7). It sets $87 to $BB, clears $011B-$013E and draws panel picture 0 at both of its places (DrawUiImageRecord, $AFE1, with A = 0 and X = 0, then 1). It builds no scene or wall data. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and the drawing routine's scratch.

Take the exit at the edge of the current area; MainTick calls it once a tick, and it does nothing while $0234 is non-zero. Inputs: $0234, current area $A2, player position $54 (across) and $55 (down), and the exit thresholds at $8FF7. Outputs: when the player is at an edge (Y below 9, Y $BD or more, X $F7 or more, or X below 2) the position becomes a place on the area's edge, counted clockwise from the top left: a quarter of the distance along the edge, plus 0 on the top, $3D on the right, $6A on the bottom and $A7 on the left. The first exit of the area's group in $8FF7 whose threshold is above that place is installed through InstallSceneStateRecordX ($8FA9), which moves the player to the destination area and position, or sets the level-exit request $02AF=$FF when the destination is $FF. Away from the edges it returns without change. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and the installed area/player state.

Install record 0, the level's starting place, as the selected spawn: it loads X with 0 and falls into InstallSceneStateRecordX, whatever the current room. In Mansion record 0 is area 1 at X $58, Y $5A, heading 3. Its one caller is InitSceneBuffers ($8BC8). Inputs: none. Outputs: $0278=0, and the area, player position, heading, command and redraw latches from record 0. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and the installed area/player state.

Install the Mansion scene-state/spawn record selected by X.
Inputs: X indexes parallel area, player-coordinate, heading, and command-state arrays at $9011/$902B/$9045/$905F; callers have already resolved the transition variant and any $0234 gate.
Outputs: A $FF area byte sets $02AF=$FF and returns; otherwise stores X in $0278 and installs area $A2, player coordinates $54/$55/$028E/$028F/$74, heading $68/$69, derived pose $65, command $81, and redraw latches $02A9/$02B8.
Clobbers: A, X, processor flags, $0278, $02AF on the sentinel path, and the installed area/player/redraw state; Y is preserved.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Load the selected Mansion spawn record into active area, player-position, facing, and transition state
Inputs: $0278 = selected record index; parallel Mansion area, X, Y, and packed facing/state tables
Outputs: $A2 = area; $54/$028E = X; $55/$74/$028F = Y; $68/$69 = heading; $65 = $10 or $11 facing-image selector; $81 = packed byte shifted right four; $02A9/$02B8 = $FF; A = $FF; X = selected index
Clobbers: A, X, and processor flags; Y is preserved

26 bytes of exit thresholds. Byte 0 belongs to no area: the scans start at byte 1, and entry 0 of the four tables that follow is the level's start position. Then comes a group for each area, closed by $FF. The routine that finds the exit the player is walking through skips a group for each area before the current one, turns the player's place on the edge of the play window into one number running clockwise round it from the top left, and takes the first value in the group above that number, the closing $FF included. The same index then selects the exit's destination in the four tables that follow.

26 exits, $9011-$902A: the area it leads to, or $FF for the way out of the level (entry 24, the first exit of area 12's group), which sets the level-exit request $02AF instead of moving the player. Values: 0, 1, 2, 0, 3, 4, 2, 7, 5, 2, 6, 3, 7, 3, 9, 8, 6, 7, 10, 7, 12, 9, 12, 9, 255, 10.
26 exits, $905F-$9078: the heading in the low three bits, and a command in the high nibble. Values: 3, 1, 7, 5, 5, 7, 1, 5, 7, 3, 3, 3, 5, 1, 3, 1, 1, 5, 1, 5, 1, 5, 1, 5, 255, 5.

The player's death, once the fall is over: it clears $F2, crumbles the sprites away (DissolveSpriteImages, $B01A), lowers the sprite curtain over the play window again (AnimateStatusPanelReveal, $1F75), waits 25 ticks (WaitEngineTicks, $A553), clears the play window ($140E), sets the background to black and takes one from the lives, item 26's flag at $03F2. The caller tests the Z flag that the DEC leaves: with no lives left it spends a spare life, item 8, if the player has one, and otherwise the game is over. Clobbers: A, X, Y and flags.
Impose a short fixed CPU delay. Inputs: none. Outputs: X ends at zero after 128 countdown iterations. Clobbers: X and flags; A and Y are preserved.

Reset The Mansion's transient control, actor, object, animation, and AI state to its fixed entry sentinels when the level starts or restarts: its one caller is InitSceneBuffers ($8BCF), not the area set-up. Inputs: No register arguments; the Mansion playable occupant and shared zero-page workspace are active. Outputs: Stores $FF to $6C, $02B8, and $84; stores zero to $78, $02AF, $61, $63, $64, $66, $9F, $B3, $B6, $B4, $72, $F2, $7D, $BF, and $0279; stores $AC to $86; A returns $AC. Clobbers: A, N, and Z plus the listed RAM state; X, Y, C, and V are preserved.

Sample and normalize gameplay input and process edge-triggered interface controls for The Mansion. Inputs: active-low control-port-2 state, control-port-1/keyboard state, keyboard-select table `$1DA5`, previous edge latches, and current interface state. Outputs: `$7C` bits 0–4 from control-port-2 direction/fire and bit 5 from the POTX threshold, raw keyboard rows `$0260-$0267`, edge latches `$02AA-$02AE/$02BF`, and phase interface/action state. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and scanner/interface scratch. Hardware: writes `$FF`, keyboard-row masks, and `$80` to CIA 1 port A `$DC00`; reads `$DC00`, CIA 1 port B `$DC01`, and SID POTX `$D419`; on the F1 edge that switches the music off (`$AA` flipped to zero) it clears SID registers `$D400-$D417`.

Text "MODE  ", drawn by the call at $9231 that comes before it: column 17, row 20, colours $03 and $E6, then 6 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The second space, at $923D, is a placeholder: the instruction at $922E writes the mode $03F3 (0 to 2) plus $1C into it before the call, so the line reads MODE 1, MODE 2 or MODE 3. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $923F.
Text 9234 plus 9, the address the instruction at $922E writes: byte 9 of the table at $9234.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "MODE" at $923E, and the routine that called it at $9231 goes on.

Initial sequence byte zero and the current-value indexed base for the hidden-input recognizer at $9270. Together with the next-byte alias $928C it stores 19 values $928B-$929D; the scanner advances $BF only when normalized input matches the expected change. After the 18th matched change it sets $02AF=$FF, the request to end the level.
Expected next value of the 19-byte control sequence beginning at $928B, read with the current progress X at $9275. This is an overlapping indexed base, not another allocated array.

Apply the entrance rules for the exit the player arrived by and for the current area. Inputs: $0278, the exit record the player arrived by (an index into the tables at $9011 on), and the current area $A2. Outputs: the entrance animation's kind and length from the list at $931E go to $0293/$0294 (kind 0 when $0278 is not listed); exit $17 sets $74=$98 and $EF=$FF; in area $0D with item flag $03E9 set, the first collision coordinate is copied ($FA89 to $FA8B) and it returns; otherwise InitializeRoomSpecificEntranceState installs the AI scripts and sprite colours of areas $0A, $0E, $0F, $10 and $11. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and AI-script state. Hardware: writes the sprite multicolour registers $D025/$D026 directly in areas $0A, $0E, $10 and $11.

The Mansion's own entrance rules, with the area number in Y. At the start of the level (spawn record $0278 zero: area 0, X 34, Y 0) the player arrives hanging from the helicopter: it starts the helicopter's animation $C9BD in the second actor's slot, sets the sprite multicolours $D025 and $D026 to 11 and 15 (dark and light grey), $F8 to $0C, which ServiceEnemyBoundaryLatch at $9BC4 acts on, and $74 to $C0, and sets $EF, $B1 (the player holding on), $0234 (no area transitions), $58 and $61 to $FF. Elsewhere: area 9, once flag $03EB is set (item 19, the lights on), draws scene $BD45, the switch in its on position; area 12 starts the second actor's animation $CAC8, or $CAC1 once flag $03ED is set (item 21, ObjectTurnAreaTwelveActor at $BD28). Any other area returns.

The Mansion's entrance-animation list, three bytes an entry as in Central Park's (the spawn record the player arrived by, the kind of entrance, how many animation steps it lasts), ending with $FF: arriving by record 2 (area 2) plays kind 1 for 15 steps, and by record 10 (area 6, X 69, Y 79) kind 5, which only The Mansion has (AdvanceBoundarySequence at $9CCA). Kind 5's length byte, 2, is never used: AdvanceBoundarySequence clears the kind $0293 at once ($9CDC) and plays animation $C091 without counting $0294 down.
The second byte of each entrance-animation entry, the kind, read with X stepping by three.

The third byte of each entrance-animation entry, its length in animation steps (AdvanceBoundarySequence counts it down once each time the player's previous animation has finished), read with the same X. Kind 5 does not use it.

Mark all eight actor slots inactive and clear their key state bytes. Inputs: none. Outputs: $61, $63, and the corresponding $0210 and $0248 slot arrays are cleared. Clobbers: A is zero, Y exits as $FF, and flags change; X is preserved.

Copy the 1000-byte screen-color staging image into C64 color RAM. Inputs: staging bytes $0800-$0BE7 and visible C64 I/O. Outputs: color RAM $D800-$DBE7 receives the corresponding low nybbles; the last 24 cells of the third page are harmlessly copied twice. Clobbers: A, X, and flags; X returns zero. Hardware: writes color RAM $D800-$DBE7.

Provide The Mansion's reserved per-tick runtime hook. Inputs: A normal JSR return address on the stack. Outputs: Returns immediately without changing gameplay state. Clobbers: Registers and flags are preserved; RTS consumes the normal return address.

Provide The Mansion's reserved presentation-initialization hook. Inputs: A normal JSR return address on the stack. Outputs: Returns immediately without changing presentation state. Clobbers: Registers and flags are preserved; RTS consumes the normal return address.

RTS: where The Mansion's title load points PlayNextLoadVector at $3FF6. The one call through that vector, from StartLevelLoad (engine $1405), comes once as the game starts, before any level is loaded, and goes through the engine's own JMP $0E00 there, so this RTS is never reached.

RenderConditionalSceneVariant, The Mansion's version: in area 10, while flag $03EB is clear (item 19, the switch in area 9 that ObjectLightsOn at $BD1C turns on), it draws area 11's scene in its place (A = $0B): scene 129, nine pictures on a black background, area 10 with its lights off. Area 11 is not a place: no spawn record leads there. Any other time it draws the plain scene of the current area.

When the player's level-condition latch is active and no player animation script is running, force zero health and install the facing-specific terminal animation
Inputs: condition latch $B6, player animation-pointer high byte $61, and facing byte $69; animation streams begin at $BF62 and $BF56
Outputs: sets player health $0229=0 and tail-installs one of the two terminal animation streams; otherwise returns unchanged
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and the state changed by InstallAnimation

Hide the parts of an actor's sprites that are behind the current area's foreground pictures, then stage the sprites. Inputs: X is the first sprite slot to process (0 for the player, 4 for the other actor, or an auxiliary slot); it works up to slot 3, or slot 7 when X is 4 or more. A is the actor's depth ($74 or $74,X), compared with byte 1 of each 4-byte record in the area's list (pointers at $963D, an $FF ends a list; a record is a picture's scene index, a depth, a column and a row). Outputs: for each drawn slot ($0218 bit 4 or 6 set, $0210 non-zero), every record whose depth is at least A is tested by TestSceneConditionRecord ($9440): where the picture overlaps the 24-by-21 sprite, the sprite's pixel pairs under the picture's non-zero pixels are cleared and $0218 bit 4 is set. Then, with interrupts off, each slot with $0218 bit 6 gets its position, pointer ($30 or $38 plus the slot) and colour bits staged in $0240, $0258 and $0250, and $0210 is copied to $0248. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and masking scratch.

Mask one foreground picture out of a sprite slot. Inputs: ($ED) points at the area's list of 4-byte records (scene index, depth, column, row) and Y at the depth byte of one of them; $1F is the sprite slot, and $F4/$F6 and $F5 its X (low and high bytes) and Y. Outputs: the record's picture is placed at column x 8 and row x 8 + $1A, with the width and height from its header byte; if it does not overlap the 24-by-21 sprite the routine returns at once, otherwise it sets bit 4 of the slot's $0218 and clears, in the slot's sprite image, every pixel pair that lies under a non-zero pixel pair of the picture. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $04-$07, $1C/$1D, $21/$22, $25/$26, $8C/$8D, $D7-$DB and the slot's sprite image.

24 entries: eight zeroes, eight ones and eight twos. $956E/$9584/$959A/$95B0 use clipped horizontal pixel X to select the destination byte within a three-byte sprite row. Paired with the clearing masks at $9624; X advances two hires pixels per multicolor source pair.

24 entries: $3F,$3F,$CF,$CF,$F3,$F3,$FC,$FC repeated for three sprite bytes. The scene-condition renderer ANDs these into the selected sprite-row byte whenever the corresponding source pixel pair is nonzero. This removes a two-bit pair, selected jointly with the byte-offset lookup at $960C. Ends at $963B; $963C is a zero byte between it and the pointer directory, which no instruction reads.

17 pointers to condition lists, one for each area by number: the routine that tests the actors against their area's conditions reads the pair for twice the area number. area 0: $965F; area 1: $96C4; area 2: $9711; area 3: $974E; area 4: $977F; area 5: $97C8; area 6: $97D5; area 7: $980E; area 8: $989B; area 9: $98B4; area 10: $98F5; area 11: $9946; area 12: $9947; area 13: $9983; area 14: $9983; area 15: $9983; area 16: $9983.
ConditionListPointers plus 1, the address the instruction at $9398 reads with Y as the index: the high byte of each word of the table, the index counting in pairs from the low byte.

Condition list for area 0, $965F-$96C3: 25 four-byte entries, then $FF. Each entry is a picture's scene index, the largest depth of the actor (the caller's parameter, $F7) at which the picture is tested against it, and the column and row where the picture is placed; the picture's size comes from its header.

Walls of area 0, $9984-$99C8, ending with $FF. The compiler finds them by skipping 0 lists from $9984, and turns each chain (a start X and Y, then for each segment a direction byte and a length byte, and a third byte, a script command, when the length has bit 0 set; bit 0 of the direction ends the chain) into six-byte records at $FA89 for the movement tests.

ServiceEnemyBoundaryLatch, The Mansion's version, called from MainTick every pass: it does nothing unless $F8 is $0C, which the entrance rules set at the start of the level, and $B1 is non-zero. $B1 is $FF while the player hangs from the helicopter and $7F once they let go.

Let go ($B1 positive): the player drops 8 pixels a pass. Over the landing spot (X from $16 to $30) they land at Y $3D: $74 becomes $C0, animation $BFB0 plays (frames 44, 45 and 44) and $F8, $B1 and $0234 are cleared, so play goes on. Anywhere else they go on falling, and at Y $60 they die: $B6 is set to $FF and $F8 and $61 are cleared.
over the landing spot?
fallen to Y $60: dead

Holding on ($B1 negative). Once the helicopter's animation has ended ($63 zero) it clears $F8 and $61. Otherwise the player hangs 20 pixels left of the helicopter ($56) and 40 above it ($57); while the helicopter is less than 20 from the left edge nothing is drawn and the controls are not read. Pushing down or pressing fire ($7C & $12) sets $B1 to $7F, and the player lets go.
down or fire: let go

Draws the player in frame 83 (ComposeSprites with X = 0, Y = $53, also stored in $65, and A = $40), tests the scene conditions at a fixed depth of $74 (the immediate value, not the byte $74) and sets $58 to $FF.

FlashAlarmLamps, called from MainTick every pass, a call Central Park's MainTick does not make: it redraws the lamp of the current area with its colour changed, at most every 12 counts of the interrupt counter $E2 (the last time kept in $03EE), while the alarm is ringing ($03EA has any of its low seven bits set). Once the alarm is switched off (item 24, ObjectSwitchOffAlarm at $BD3A, sets $03F0 to $FF) it flashes 16 more times, at most every 3 counts, decrementing $03F0 at each flash from $FF down to $EF, and then stops.

Looks the current area up in the lamp table at $9CBA (sorted by area, so it stops at the first larger one), flips $03EF between 0 and 1 and writes $11 (0) or $C1 (1) into byte 5 of the area's lamp scene, its third colour swap, before drawing it (RenderSceneRecordTree). $11 leaves the lamp's white as it is; $C1 paints it medium grey (12).

The alarm lamps, three bytes an entry, sorted by area and ending with $FF: the area, then the address of its lamp scene, low byte first. Area 2: $BD59. Area 3: $BD63. Area 7: $BD6D. Area 8: $BD77. Area 9: $BD81.
The lamp table plus 1, read at $9C99 with X at an entry's start: the low byte of the lamp scene.
The lamp table plus 2, read at $9C9E: the high byte of the lamp scene.

AdvanceBoundarySequence, The Mansion's version, which PlayerDriver calls at $A098: Central Park's routine at $A08A with one kind of entrance added. Nothing happens while the player's animation runs ($61), so each count below is one animation step, taken once the one before has finished. Kind 5, which only the arrival by spawn record 10 has, clears the kind $0293 at once and plays animation $C091: five steps of 4 right and 1 down (frames 8 to 12), then frame 17 moving 7 down three times. The other kinds count $0294 down and clear $0293 at zero. Kinds 0 and 1 drop the player 8 pixels a step in the falling frame for their heading, 78 or 83 (InstallDirectionalPlayerAnimation, $C999 or $C9A2), and at the last step play $BFB0 or $BFA2, by bit 2 of the heading (frames 44, 45 and 44). Kind 2 climbs 11 pixels up a step ($BFE7) and steps off the top at the last ($BFFC). Kinds 3 and 4 climb 11 down a step ($C02D) and step off at the last ($C042), kind 4 dropping 8 pixels a step instead once fewer than 6 steps are left. The Mansion's entrance list uses only kinds 1 and 5.

Conditionally dispatch the pending script command through the Mansion target-minus-one table
Inputs: command/state bytes $80/$81 and player animation-pointer high byte $61; $80 low six bits select the command; the target-minus-one words start at $9D6E and are read from the base $9D6C with X = twice the command
Outputs: when $81 is negative and the bit-6/$61 gate admits it, transfers to the selected command handler by RTS dispatch; command zero or a failed gate returns normally

RTS completing the stack-built dispatch at $9D65. The high-byte indexed load uses this address as its base with X=2*command, so nonzero commands read the high bytes of target-minus-one words beginning at $9D6E. 57 words, each the routine for one script command, from command 1 up less one: the dispatcher pushes it and returns into it. Return at once, for the script commands that have no action. Its RTS returns to the code that called ScriptDispatch: the address the dispatcher pushed was used up by the RTS at $9D6D that jumped here. Inputs and outputs: none. Clobbers: nothing.

Script command 13: plays the player's facing animation four times through, running the engine until each one ends (RepeatScriptRuntimeFrames, A = 4), then, where Central Park runs its scripted coordinate sequence with X = $F8 and Y = 4, calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $A064, so the player loses two points of energy. No wall in The Mansion carries command 13, and the walls are the only source of commands, so it never runs in this level.

When command bit 0 is set, run seven scripted cycles and enter the common death-latch tail; otherwise only clear the command.

Outputs: Armed path calls $9F1A with A=7 then writes $B6=$FF; unarmed path clears $81 without damage.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $81, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and on the armed path $B6.

Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $81, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and on the armed path $B6.

Run The Mansion's fixed animation at $C02D the requested number of times, run the finishing animation at $C042 once, then synchronize three engine-tick stamps. Inputs: A is a nonzero repetition count; animation streams $C02D and $C042, actor state, the blocking runtime loop, and resident tick-snapshot helper $11F1 are active. Outputs: Each $C02D cycle is installed and serviced until $61 clears; $C042 is then installed and serviced once; finally $026C, $026E, and $0277 receive the current engine tick $E2 and A returns that tick. Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, transient stack contents, animation/runtime state, and $026C/$026E/$0277. Hardware: Through the blocking runtime loop, advances sprite/display state and reads controls; this wrapper and the $11F1 timer-snapshot tail perform no direct I/O.

Install an animation and run the blocking script runtime loop. Inputs: A:X is the animation pointer and the actor context is valid. Outputs: the animation is installed and the runtime loop completes. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and runtime state. Hardware: changes sprite presentation indirectly through the engine.

Run script-time engine frames until the active actor or action completes. Inputs: an installed animation and valid runtime state. Outputs: enemy AI, auxiliary sprites, input, and animation state advance until $61 clears. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and broad frame scratch. Hardware: changes sprite and display state indirectly and reads input through the called joystick poller.

Advance the player's and then the enemy's animation by one eligible engine step, at most once a tick. Inputs: tick $E2 and timer slot 2 ($026A, interval 1 at $A142); both actors' animation state. Outputs: when no tick has passed since the last call the gate at $A12C returns straight to RunScriptRuntimeLoop; otherwise AnimationInterpreter ($A464, X=0) steps the player's animation, and ScheduleEnemyAnimation ($A44F) steps the enemy's when its own tick has advanced. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation scratch.

Execute a scripted action for a fixed number of completed animation cycles. Inputs: A is the repetition count and actor facing and animation state are valid. Outputs: the count is exhausted and scripted state advances. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, stack, and $0234. Hardware: changes sprite and display state indirectly.

Script command 56, which two walls in area 4 carry (command byte $B8, so they also stop the player): climbing down with the rope. It sets the player's action $6D to $0C, $74 to 4 and $EF to $FF. When $70 is zero, the player faces neither heading 3 nor heading 5, and the selected item $0279 is 15, the rope, it plays animation $C04D (frames 74, 75, 76 and 75 four times, 11 pixels down each, 44 pixels in all), whose last step raises event 22, which leaves the area by transition variant 1, and clears $81. Otherwise the player falls 48 pixels at depth 4 and dies (FallPlayerAtDepthX).
Script command 48, which walls in areas 0 and 1 carry: the player falls 31 pixels at depth 4 and dies.
Script command 49, which walls in area 0 carry: the player falls 48 pixels at depth 4 and dies.
Script command 50, which walls in area 0 carry: when bit 0 of $81 is set, the player falls 48 pixels at depth $80 and dies.
Script command 51, which walls in area 0 carry: the player falls at depth $E0 until they reach Y $BD, and dies.
Script command 52, which a wall in area 0 carries: the player falls 40 pixels at depth $50 and dies.

Script command 55, which a wall in area 0 carries: with the player's X at $70 or more they drop 24 pixels at depth $50 and land: $B6, $81 and $0234 are cleared again after the fall. Further left they fall 64 pixels at depth 4 and die.
Never reached: no table entry or jump leads here. With bit 0 of $81 set it would make the player fall 31 pixels at whatever depth X held.
Script command 54, which a wall in area 1 carries: the player drops 46 pixels at depth $30 and lands ($B6, $81 and $0234 cleared after the fall), then leaves the area by transition variant 0.
Script command 53, which walls in areas 0 and 1 carry: the player falls 30 pixels at depth $40 and dies.
Never reached: no table entry or jump leads here. It is The Office's command 47 (ScriptFallFortyEight at $9B6E there): a fall of 48 pixels at depth 2.
FallPlayerAtDepthX: X is the depth, A how far to fall. It stores X in $74, sets $EF to $FF and goes on into FallPlayer.

FallPlayer: A is how far to fall. It keeps the time in $022E and sets $0234 to $FF, and then, for every two or more counts of the interrupt counter $E2, moves the player down 4 pixels a count and draws them in the falling frame for their heading from $A034, testing the scene conditions at depth $74. Between steps it runs ScheduleEnemyAnimation and RuntimeNoOpHook. Once a step's move is more than the distance still to fall, or the player has reached Y $BD, it sets $B6 to $FF and the player dies, unless the caller clears it again. The step that ends the fall has already moved the player, so they fall a little past the distance: 48 pixels in steps of 8 end after 56.
The two falling frames: 78 when the player's heading plus 2 has bit 2 clear, 83 when it is set (read at $A003 with X from the heading).

Install one of two player-animation descriptors selected from the current facing direction. Inputs: Player facing $69 and Mansion animation descriptors $C999 and $C9A2. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation state through the tail-called installer.

No wall in The Mansion carries command 31, and the walls are the only source of commands, so it never runs in this level.

Sets X to $07 and Y to 2 and goes on to ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $A064, which ignores them: Central Park's scripted coordinate sequence, which would have read them, is not in this level.

Sets X to $0E and Y to 0 and goes on to ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $A064, which ignores them: Central Park's scripted coordinate sequence, which would have read them, is not in this level.
