Object record 00 plus 2, the address the instruction at $BBF7 reads with X as the index: byte 2 of whichever object record the index points at.
Object record 00 plus 3, the address the instruction at $BBF0 reads with X as the index: byte 3 of whichever object record the index points at.
Object record 00 plus 4, the address the instruction at $BBFC reads with X as the index: byte 4 of whichever object record the index points at.
Object record 00 plus 5, the address the instructions at $BDCD and $BE35 read with X as the index: byte 5 of whichever object record the index points at.
Object record 00 plus 6, the address the instructions at $BDD2, $BE1D and $BE3A read with X as the index: byte 6 of whichever object record the index points at.
Object record 00 plus 7, the address the instructions at $BC2C and $BE42 read with X as the index: byte 7 of whichever object record the index points at.
Object record 00 plus 8, the address the instructions at $BC31, $BE22 and $BE47 read with X as the index: byte 8 of whichever object record the index points at.
Object record 00 plus 9, the address the instruction at $BC01 reads with X as the index: byte 9 of whichever object record the index points at.
Object record 00 plus 10, the address the instruction at $BC06 reads with X as the index: byte 10 of whichever object record the index points at.
Object record 00 plus 11, the address the instructions at $BBD8, $BDC5 and $BE27 read with X as the index: byte 11 of whichever object record the index points at.
Object record 00 plus 12, the address the instruction at $BBD3 reads with X as the index: byte 12 of whichever object record the index points at.
Object record 00 plus 13, the address the instruction at $BBE0 reads with X as the index: byte 13 of whichever object record the index points at.

Object record 1, $BCD5-$BCE2: area 5; the player must stand at X 171 to 184 and Y 111 to 120, facing 1, with action 0; scene $BD8B draws it in the room, scene $BDA1 redraws the spot once it is taken, and it is item 15.
Object record 2, $BCE3-$BCF0: area 8; the player must stand at X 144 to 156 and Y 86 to 89, facing 1, with action 0; nothing is drawn in the room, the routine at $BD3A runs first, and it is item 24.

Object record 3, $BCF1-$BCFE: area 9; the player must stand at X 186 to 199 and Y 107 to 111, facing 7, with action 0; nothing is drawn in the room, scene $BD45 redraws the spot once it is taken, the routine at $BD1C runs first, and it is item 19.

Object record 4, $BCFF-$BD0C: area 9; the player must stand at X 186 to 199 and Y 107 to 111, facing 7, with action 0; nothing is drawn in the room, scene $BD52 redraws the spot once it is taken, the routine at $BD22 runs first, and it is item 20.

Object record 5, $BD0D-$BD1A: area 12; the player must stand at X 147 to 157 and Y 102 to 107, facing 7, with action 0; nothing is drawn in the room, the routine at $BD28 runs first, and it is item 21.
$FF in place of an area: the end of the 6 object records that start at $BCC7.

ObjectLightsOn: the routine object record 3 (area 9) calls. It clears flag $03EC (item 20) and returns with A zero, so ObjectEngine takes item 19: flag $03EB is set, which lights area 10 (RenderConditionalSceneVariant at $9358), scene $BD45 draws the switch on, and 500 points are added to the score ($1183 with A = 5, the hundreds digit). Records 3 and 4 share one spot, and ObjectEngine passes over a record whose item flag is set, so each use takes whichever of the two is clear: the switch goes on, off and on again, scoring 500 every time.

ObjectLightsOff: the routine object record 4 (area 9) calls. It clears flag $03EB (item 19), which turns area 10's lights off, and returns with A zero, so ObjectEngine takes item 20 (flag $03EC), draws scene $BD52, the switch off, and adds 500 points to the score ($1183 with A = 5, the hundreds digit).

ObjectTurnAreaTwelveActor: the routine object record 5 (area 12) calls. It starts animation $CAD5 in the second actor's slot (frames 105, 104 and 103, a move of 51 left and 36 up, frames 104 and 105, then on into $CACD, frames 100 to 102 over and over), copies the first wall's start X ($FA89) into its end X ($FA8B), so that the first wall of area 12, the one whose command 57 kills the player, no longer stops them, and returns with A zero, so ObjectEngine takes item 21 (flag $03ED). On later visits the entrance rules start the actor at its new place ($CAC1); they do not remove the wall again.

ObjectSwitchOffAlarm: the routine object record 2 (area 8) calls. It keeps only bit 7 of the alarm $03EA, which stops the lamps flashing, and returns with A zero, so ObjectEngine takes item 24: $03F0 becomes $FF, the lamps flash fast 16 times (FlashAlarmLamps), and command 47 no longer sets the alarm off. A non-zero $03EA is what quadruples enemies' blows, so once the alarm has rung, bit 7 keeps them at four times their strength.

Object scene $BD45-$BD51, which object record 3 draws once the object is taken, and the entrance rules draw on entering area 9 while flag $03EB is set ($92FB): 3 placed scenes (9, 9, 29) in the same three-byte placement format as a composite scene, ending with $FF.
Object scene $BD52-$BD58, which object record 4 draws once the object is taken: 2 placed scenes (9, 9) in the same three-byte placement format as a composite scene, ending with $FF.

The lamp scene of area 2, which FlashAlarmLamps draws: scene 69, the lamp, at column 7, row 3, with three colour swaps ($1B, $1C, then $11 or $C1, the byte FlashAlarmLamps rewrites), then scene 76 at the same place, ending with $FF.
The lamp scene of area 3: scene 69 at column 17, row 2, with the same three swaps, then scene 76 there, ending with $FF.
The lamp scene of area 7: scene 69 at column 18, row 1, with the same three swaps, then scene 76 there, ending with $FF.
The lamp scene of area 8: scene 69 at column 24, row 2, with the same three swaps, then scene 76 there, ending with $FF.
The lamp scene of area 9: scene 69 at column 17, row 2, with the same three swaps, then scene 76 there, ending with $FF.
Object scene $BD8B-$BDA0, which object record 0 draws: 7 placed scenes (67, 67, 67, 67, 67, 67, 68) in the same three-byte placement format as a composite scene, ending with $FF.
Object scene $BDA1-$BDB1, which object records 0 and 1 draw once the object is taken: 4 placed scenes (75, 75, 75, 75) in the same three-byte placement format as a composite scene, ending with $FF.

Draw the picture of the first object record of the current area ($A2) whose item is still in place. It scans the 14-byte records from $BCC7 to the $FF that ends them, passing over those of other areas, those whose item's flag ($03D8 plus the record's byte 11) is set, and those with no picture (bytes 5 and 6 of the record, a high byte of 0), and tail-enters the scene renderer ($885A) with the first one left in $02/$03: at most one picture is drawn. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $02/$03, and the renderer's scratch when it draws.

Expire a displayed inactive object after 100 engine ticks. Inputs: creation or display tick $A0 and current tick $E2. Outputs: the object remains or is cleared and its UI is refreshed. Clobbers: A, flags, and the clear helper's clobbers on expiry. Hardware: changes UI or display memory on expiry.

Remove the inactive-object display and redraw its status image. Inputs: current inactive-object and UI state. Outputs: $A0 is cleared and the corresponding UI image is rendered. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and renderer scratch. Hardware: changes hardware-visible UI bitmap, screen, and color RAM.

The RTS that ends the Mansion playable phase's inactive-object expiry check. The branches at $BDE3 and $BDE7 come here when the delay has not elapsed or no inactive object is pending, and ClearInactiveObjectAndRefreshUi also ends here after redrawing the panel's image.
Inputs: A valid return address is on the stack.
Outputs: Returns; on the two branch paths nothing has been cleared or redrawn.
Clobbers: Registers, flags, object state, and memory are preserved; RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.

Periodically render the alternating active-state image for the first eligible object in the current area
Inputs: timer slot 5; phase counter $A9; current area $A2; 14-byte records at $BCC7; persistent active bytes $03D8,Y; two active scene pointers in record bytes 5-6 and 7-8
Outputs: on an admitted tick decrements $A9, selects one of the two active pointers by $A9 bit 0, loads it into $02/$03, and tail-enters the recursive renderer; clears $A9 and returns when no eligible object remains
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $A9, $02/$03, and scene-renderer scratch on a render path
